# [USBD05] Instantiate the Relational Model in Oracle

* **Priority:** High
* **Story Points:** 3 (size S, as estimated on the project board)
* **Module / Component:** `Database` / `Physical Model`
* **Status:** In Review (`database/ddl.sql` in versions 1 and 2 and `database/seed.sql` in versions 1, 2 and 3, run on Oracle FreeSQL without errors; 12 / 12 validation tests passed; review by another team member and final sign-off pending)

---

## 👤 User Story Description

**As a** Product Owner
**I want to** have the relational model instantiated in an Oracle SGBD using SQL DDL code generated by an appropriate tool
**So that** the database is ready to store data and the model's correctness can be verified with real data on Oracle FreeSQL

## 💬 Customer Specifications & Clarifications

* **Requirements doc (USBD05):** the relational model must be instantiated in an Oracle SGBD using the SQL DDL code generated by an appropriate tool.
* **Requirements doc (USBD05 acceptance criteria):** all tables in the database must be populated with data; the inserted data should allow verification that the model fulfils the requirements; it will be shown on Oracle FreeSQL.
* **Requirements doc (USBD04 acceptance criteria):** the model must be complete (an ER diagram and all constraints), so that the physical model script for Oracle RDMS can be automatically generated by a specific tool or an LLM.
* **Requirements doc (NFR02):** the database is a remote relational DBMS; all database operations must be done through an API of PL/SQL functions; the DAO pattern must be used for JDBC.
* **Requirements doc (NFR01):** the validation of business rules must be followed during data registration and updating, so the constraints of the DDL must reflect the business rules.
* **Clarification (client sessions, database in Sprint 1):** an in-memory H2 database is accepted to meet the non-functional requirements of Sprint 1. Oracle is planned for later sprints (to be confirmed). This story still instantiates the model in Oracle, as the requirements document asks.
* **Clarification (client sessions, scope):** the proof of concept covers a single shopping center (NorteShopping) in this sprint.
* **Clarification (client sessions, orders):** orders are final once confirmed and paid, and cannot be changed after payment.
* **Clarification (BDDAD teacher, requirements):** the requirements of the data model come from the whole requirements document (all the user stories) and from the client clarifications.
* **Clarification (BDDAD teacher, iterative work):** LLMs and any other tools may be used, but the repository must contain evidence of iterative and incremental development, with several versions of the artefacts. The scripts of this story are therefore committed in several versions, not only in a final one.
* **Clarification (BDDAD teacher, IDs):** automatic generation of IDs is a bad idea when test data has to be injected. The seed data uses explicit IDs.
* **Clarification (BDDAD teacher, prices):** changing the price of a product must not affect previous transactions, and a serious retail system keeps a price history. Not respecting this is a mistake with no excuse.
* **Clarification (BDDAD teacher, passwords):** storing unencrypted passwords in the database is a mistake with no excuse. The teacher thinks storing passwords is not even necessary; if the model stores them, it must be done properly (hashed or encrypted).
* **Decision (location of the scripts):** `database/ddl.sql` (structure) and `database/seed.sql` (data). The team can change the folder if needed.
* **Decision (IDs in the DDL):** the identifiers are inserted explicitly by the seed script, so the DDL does not use `GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` (it does not accept explicit values). Whether a key also gets a sequence for future inserts is decided together with USBD04.
* **Decision (credentials):** the Oracle FreeSQL credentials are never committed to the repository.
* **Decision (DDL generation, confirmed by the team):** the DDL is generated by an LLM (Claude Code) from the ER diagram and the constraints of USBD04 (the diagram is in PlantUML, which Oracle SQL Developer Data Modeler cannot import), reviewed manually and executed on Oracle FreeSQL. The evidence of the generation (inputs, instructions, checks and manual review) is kept in `database/ddl-generation.md`, the versions of the scripts are kept in the repository history, and the use of the tool is declared in the generative AI usage declaration on the project board.
* **Assumption (seed data):** the seed data must be meaningful, without placeholder values (e.g., no `"name1"`, `"test"`), and every table of the model (16 tables) has at least one row. It covers NorteShopping and at least one more shopping location (only to prove that the model supports several shopping locations, as the requirements document describes), levels with and without a robot station (including a decimal level), robots in every state (including refrigerated units), a store without merchant (and, by rule R17, without products), products that require refrigeration and products that do not, customers, orders in different statuses (including an order split into sub-orders), and routes of orders and of sub-orders. It also includes a product whose price changed, to prove the price history. Only the real data of NorteShopping that is known is used as real; the rest is fictional and labelled as such in the script.
* **Decision (seed version 3):** version 2 of the seed broke rule R17 of the relational model (a store without a merchant has no products): the store without merchant sold a product. Version 3 gives that store a merchant and adds a new store without merchant and without products, with its own area and vertices. The counts change to AREA 16, AREA_VERTEX 64, MERCHANT 5 and STORE 8; the other tables are unchanged.
* **Assumption (units):** weight in kg, volume in litres, prices in euros, distance in metres and duration in seconds. The units are not defined in the requirements document.
* **Assumption (execution order):** the DDL starts with a block that drops the 16 tables (children first), so it can be run again on the same schema. The tables are then created in dependency order: RETAILER, SHOPPING_LOCATION, SHOPPING_LEVEL, AREA, AREA_VERTEX, MERCHANT, STORE, PRODUCT, PRODUCT_PRICE, CUSTOMER, ROBOT_STATION, ROBOT, CUSTOMER_ORDER, SUB_ORDER, ORDER_LINE and ROUTE. The seed script empties the tables (children first) and inserts the rows parents first.
* **Out of Scope:** PL/SQL API functions and triggers (they belong to the LAPR3 stories), so the business rules of the model that need them (R1 to R10, R16 and R17) are not enforced by the DDL, and the seed data respects them; Java JDBC code; route planning.

## 🔒 Non-Functional Requirements & Security

* **NFR01 (Business Rules):** constraints in the DDL (NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK, FK) must reflect all the business rules identified in USBD03 and USBD04.
* **NFR02 (Database):** remote Oracle SGBD; structure ready to be accessed via PL/SQL API and JDBC in future sprints.
* **NFR05 (Documentation):** must follow the team documentation standards.
* **Security:** the Oracle FreeSQL credentials are not committed; if the model stores passwords, they are never in plain text (neither in the DDL nor in the seed data).
* **Not applicable:** performance and authorisation NFRs do not directly apply to this story.

## 🔗 Found Out Dependencies

### Upstream Dependencies (Required before starting)
* **[USBD04] Relational Model (Margarida Sá):** the ER diagram and all constraints must be finalised before the DDL can be generated. The model is available in `doc/relational-model/relational-model.puml` (version 2, with 16 tables and the price history), so this story is **no longer blocked**.
* **[USBD03] Conceptual Domain Model:** the physical model must be traceable to the conceptual model; any entity not in USBD03 must be justified.

### Parallel Dependencies
* **Generative AI usage declaration:** the use of an LLM to generate the DDL must be declared (tool, purpose and parts supported).

### Downstream Dependencies (Impacted by this story)
* **[USLP03] Shopping App skeleton and [USLP04] List Available Stores:** the `Level` and `Store` tables created here are the ones the Shopping App will query via JDBC.
* **[USLP06] Import of GeoJSON data:** the back-office will import into the tables created here.
* **All ESINF stories (USEI01–USEI05):** these process data in memory in Sprint 1, but the table structure here defines what will be persisted in future sprints.

## Edge Cases

* **DDL execution order:** tables with FK dependencies must be created after the tables they reference; the script must handle this order or the team must adjust it manually.
* **Circular FK references:** the relational model has no circular dependencies, so no deferred constraints are needed.
* **Oracle-specific syntax:** the DDL must be Oracle-compatible (use `NUMBER`, `VARCHAR2`, `DATE`; avoid MySQL/PostgreSQL-specific syntax).
* **Constraint naming:** all primary key, unique, foreign key and check constraints must have explicit names (e.g., `PK_ROBOT`, `FK_ROBOT_STATION`) to facilitate error diagnosis and future alterations. `NOT NULL` constraints are declared inline in the column definition and are named by Oracle (`SYS_C...`), so they are not counted as named constraints.* **Explicit IDs:** the seed script inserts the identifiers itself; a column that rejects explicit values (e.g., `GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY`) must not be used.
* **Seed data referential integrity:** INSERT statements must respect the FK order, with parent rows before child rows; no INSERT must violate an active FK constraint.
* **Seed data coverage:** every table must have at least one row; FK columns must reference rows that actually exist in the parent table.
* **Seed data and the rules outside the DDL:** the rules that the DDL cannot enforce (R1 to R10, R16 and R17) must still be respected by the seed data (for example, a store without a merchant has no products).
* **Price change:** updating the current price of a product must not change the price paid in previous order lines.
* **Empty result sets during demo:** if a query over the seed data returns zero rows, it must be justified (e.g., a status value that no seed order currently holds).

## 🧪 Functional Tests / Validation

Since this is a database instantiation deliverable, "testing" here means **SQL validation queries** run on Oracle FreeSQL rather than JUnit tests (the same cases as in the [qa-readme](./qa-readme.md)):

| Scenario ID | Validation Query / Check                                                                                    | Expected Result                                        |
|:------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| **TC-01**   | Run the full DDL script on a clean Oracle FreeSQL schema                                                    | No errors; all tables created                          |
| **TC-02**   | `SELECT table_name FROM user_tables ORDER BY 1;`                                                            | All USBD04 tables appear                               |
| **TC-03**   | Count the named constraints in `user_constraints` (name not starting with `SYS`) and list the ones whose status is not `ENABLED`          | All named constraints present (69) and none disabled   |
| **TC-04**   | `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM <each_table>;`                                                                        | Every table has ≥ 1 row                                |
| **TC-05**   | Query the robots of a station sorted by battery                                                             | Returns the correct robots in the correct order        |
| **TC-06**   | Query the stores of a level                                                                                 | Returns only the stores of the selected level          |
| **TC-07**   | Query the pending orders of a customer                                                                      | Returns orders with status `PENDING` for that customer |
| **TC-08**   | Insert a robot with a duplicate ID                                                                          | Oracle raises a PK violation — constraint is enforced  |
| **TC-09**   | Insert an order line referencing a non-existent product                                                     | Oracle raises a FK violation — constraint is enforced  |
| **TC-10**   | Insert a robot with a NULL battery level                                                                    | Oracle raises a NOT NULL violation                     |
| **TC-11**   | Run TC-04 to TC-07 live on Oracle FreeSQL                                                                   | All queries return the expected results; no errors     |
| **TC-12**   | Change the current price of a product that is in an existing order and query that order                     | The previous order keeps the price paid; the old price is kept in the history |
